message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 19 November 2026 23:40 to 20 November 2026 23:40 UTC (21 November 05:10 IST). **Scope:** Products.txt only, normalized and deduplicated, plus the mandatory MongoDB ecosystem sweep. Product names do not establish installed versions or configurations. The findings below include new advisories about previously disclosed CVEs, not necessarily newly discovered flaws.

### MongoDB C# driver: CVE-2026-129938
**Severity:** High in the MongoDB GitHub advisory; CVSS 4.0 9.1 (critical) in the CVE record. A crafted DNS SRV response can redirect an application using a `mongodb+srv://` connection to an attacker-controlled server, potentially exposing credentials and data. MongoDB's official driver is relevant to the listed MongoDB family. Versions 2.5.0 to before 3.14.1 are affected. The CVE was published on 19 November before this window; an Italian CSIRT alert was published on 20 November within it. [MongoDB advisory](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-6cg8-fvx8-vvmm); [CSIRT alert](https://csirt.regione.toscana.it/aggiornamenti-di-sicurezza-per-prodotti-mongodb-al05-261120-csirt-ita/).

### MongoDB Java driver: CVE-2026-129932
**Severity:** Critical, according to the 20 November CSIRT alert. A driver security restriction bypass can, under certain conditions, expose sensitive information or allow altered query results. The alert identifies MongoDB Java Driver versions 3.6.0 to before 5.13.0; this official driver is relevant to the MongoDB product family. This is a new agency report on a previously disclosed CVE, not a claim of a new discovery. [CSIRT alert and vendor references](https://csirt.regione.toscana.it/aggiornamenti-di-sicurezza-per-prodotti-mongodb-al05-261120-csirt-ita/).

### Ubuntu nginx: CVE-2026-125283, CVE-2026-123640 and CVE-2026-118899
**Severity:** Not stated in the Ubuntu notice. Ubuntu's 20 November advisory describes possible remote denial of service in certain configurations or TLS connections, and potential information disclosure from malformed ClientHello messages. Both Ubuntu and nginx are on the list; applicability varies by Ubuntu release and configuration. The advisory provides corrected package versions. These CVEs were reported earlier; this is a new Ubuntu package advisory. [Ubuntu USN-9182-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9182-1).

### Ubuntu OpenJDK: multiple vulnerabilities
**Severity:** Not stated in the Ubuntu notices. On 20 November Ubuntu issued package notices for OpenJDK 8 and CRaC JDK 17, 21 and 25. For example, CVE-2026-114939 may allow remote reading or modification of sensitive data, and CVE-2026-114938 may permit denial of service or code execution in the affected CRaC packages. Ubuntu and OpenJDK are listed. These notices provide distribution-specific fixes for previously disclosed issues. [OpenJDK 8 notice](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9181-1); [CRaC JDK 17](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9178-1); [CRaC JDK 21](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9179-1); [CRaC JDK 25](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9180-1).

**MongoDB sweep:** Reviewed MongoDB security alerts and searched for Server and mongod/mongos, Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm and App Services, official integrations and libraries, including MongoDB-owned advisories without MongoDB in their titles. Search and indexing limitations mean this is not proof of absence.

**Closing:** Promptly review affected MongoDB driver deployments given the reported severity, then check Ubuntu nginx and Java package versions and applicable vendor fixes. This search is not exhaustive.
